Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Haploid degron-based memory erasure (haploid undolorous / terminator)
ideas.description: Use haploid cells with an auto-inducible degron on FOS/JUN family members (a 'terminator' of AP-1), and deplete AP-1 at defined times after a transient stimulus. Then measure whether the stimulus-induced chromatin accessibility (ATAC-seq) and the faster transcriptional re-response persist without AP-1 (memory is AP-1-independent) or decay (AP-1 maintains it).

ideas.title: Stimulus–rest–restimulus time course with dose and interval series (testing/gamely re-challenge)
ideas.description: Give a priming stimulus, wash it out, and re-challenge after varied intervals, measuring nascent RNA (PRO-seq) and target gene induction kinetics. A memory mechanism predicts primed cells respond faster or stronger, with a decay half-life that can be compared between wild-type and AP-1 perturbed cells.

ideas.title: Single-cell live imaging of AP-1 reporters (instructor-style lineage tracking)
ideas.description: Track AP-1 activity with live reporters or a FOS-GFP knock-in across cell divisions and lineages. Test whether the active or primed state is inherited by daughter cells more than expected by chance, and whether it correlates with later responsiveness.

ideas.title: Pioneer-like binding and chromatin state profiling (hiveward: following sites over time)
ideas.description: Run CUT&RUN or ChIP for JUN/FOS and for H3K27ac and H3K4me1, together with ATAC-seq, before, during and after stimulation. Identify enhancers that stay AP-1 bound or open after the signal is gone, and test whether those sites are the ones that drive faster re-induction.

ideas.title: Targeted perturbation of memory-associated sites (CRISPR dissection)
ideas.description: Use dCas9 inhibition or activation, or motif mutagenesis, at persistently accessible AP-1 sites. Test necessity and sufficiency by asking whether editing the AP-1 motif abolishes the primed response at that locus, and whether forcing AP-1 binding in naive cells induces a primed state without a stimulus.
